title: Registration and device-enrollment data may reveal the homeowner's identity
description: During account registration and enrollment, the Home Hub may collect direct identifiers such as name, email address, phone number, account username, home address, and device ownership details. If these data are exposed to unauthorized parties or over-collected, the homeowner can be identified.
assumptions: The registration flow includes personal account details and device metadata tied to a household.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifying direct identity disclosure during collection/storage; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Enrollment metadata can link devices and account to the same household
description: Camera and sensor identifiers, serial numbers, MAC addresses, and enrollment timestamps can be linked to the newly created account, allowing correlation of multiple devices with one homeowner or household profile.
assumptions: The hub stores or transmits stable device identifiers together with account identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via stable identifiers and correlated metadata.

title: Enrollment reveals presence and composition of devices in the home
description: The set of enrolled cameras and sensors can disclose sensitive facts about the household, such as security posture, room coverage, occupancy monitoring, or whether children, elderly persons, or pets may be present based on device types.
assumptions: Device model/type and placement-related metadata are available during enrollment.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of sensitive personal information inferred from provided device data.

title: Registration data may disclose home location and household details
description: If the registration process captures installation address, timezone, Wi‑Fi SSID, locale, or support information, the Home Hub or connected services may learn the homeowner's residence and household context beyond what is necessary for setup.
assumptions: Setup may request or infer address/location-related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; threat concerns disclosure of personal attributes and location-related information.

title: Homeowner may be unaware of what personal and device data are collected during setup
description: The registration and enrollment flow may not clearly explain what account details, device identifiers, network metadata, and inferred household information are collected, how long they are retained, or with whom they are shared.
assumptions: Privacy notices or just-in-time explanations may be incomplete or absent in the setup UX.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of user awareness/transparency; exact subtree may differ.

title: Setup may collect more personal data than necessary or without valid consent/legal basis
description: The Home Hub may request excessive personal details or enroll device/network metadata not strictly required for account creation and pairing, potentially violating data minimization, purpose limitation, or consent requirements.
assumptions: The system may collect optional or secondary-use data during onboarding.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with privacy obligations; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Insufficient evidence of homeowner consent or enrollment actions
description: If the system does not create trustworthy records of registration choices, privacy notice acknowledgement, and device-enrollment actions, the homeowner may later be unable to prove what they agreed to, or the provider may be unable to demonstrate valid consent and accountability.
assumptions: Audit trails for consent and enrollment events may be weak, mutable, or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation/accountability gaps around performed actions.

title: Temporary access code can identify a specific guest or visit
description: If the Home Hub receives a unique temporary access code per guest or per booking, the code value or its successful use can identify which guest is present or attempting entry.
assumptions: Assumes temporary codes are unique or mapped to a guest, reservation, or household event.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability via unique credentials; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Entry attempt reveals guest presence and arrival time
description: Submitting the temporary access code to the Home Hub discloses that a guest is at the door at a particular time, enabling inference of presence, arrival patterns, or occupancy.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub logs or exposes code-entry events, timestamps, or unlock attempts.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for disclosure of presence/activity information.

title: Access code disclosure could expose the secret itself
description: The temporary access code is privacy-sensitive authentication data. If observed, logged in plaintext, transmitted insecurely inside the hub, or exposed through diagnostics, it could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the code may be stored, logged, displayed, or transmitted in a recoverable form.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of sensitive data/credentials; exact subtree label may differ.

title: Guest may be unable to deny having entered the code
description: If the Home Hub records the temporary code use together with time and outcome, those records can later be used as evidence that the guest attempted or gained entry, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: Assumes audit logs are retained and linked to the temporary code or guest identity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation arising from logging of actions.

title: Guest may be unaware of logging and downstream use of code-entry events
description: The guest may not understand that entering the temporary code causes collection of timestamps, failed attempts, device identifiers, or sharing with household members or service providers.
assumptions: Assumes notice is limited or absent at the point of code entry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Temporary code processing may exceed consent or expected purpose
description: The guest may provide the code solely to unlock the door, while the Home Hub may also use the event for analytics, profiling of visits, retention beyond the stay, or sharing with third parties without a proper legal basis or valid consent.
assumptions: Assumes secondary uses, extended retention, or third-party sharing are possible.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/purpose creep; exact node id may vary.

title: Repeated code use can link multiple visits or actions to the same guest
description: If the same temporary code is reused across multiple entries or correlated with other hub events, the Home Hub can link separate door-unlock actions and potentially other smart-home interactions to the same guest.
assumptions: Assumes code reuse or stable association between code and guest/booking.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability across events via a persistent identifier.

title: Event log enables linkage of household activity over time
description: A persistent local event log of motion, door, and other sensor events can be correlated across timestamps to link separate observations into detailed behavior patterns for the same household or occupants, such as routines, arrivals, departures, and room usage.
assumptions: The log stores timestamps and device/source identifiers and retains entries long enough for correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro linkage subtree numbering may vary.

title: Sensor event history can identify occupants or visitors
description: Even without explicit names, recurring motion/door event sequences in the local log may identify specific occupants, visitors, or the household itself through unique behavioral signatures and occupancy schedules.
assumptions: Event patterns are sufficiently distinctive and can be associated with known persons or a specific residence.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from stored event data.

title: Local event log discloses sensitive in-home activities
description: The stored event stream reveals occupancy, sleep/wake cycles, absences, room transitions, and other intimate household behaviors. Unauthorized access to the log would disclose sensitive personal information about people in the home.
assumptions: An attacker, insider, or secondary user can access the local datastore or backups.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node id; exact subtree numbering may differ.

title: Logging may exceed expected purpose or granularity
description: Writing all motion, door, and sensor events to a persistent local log may collect more detailed behavioral data than occupants expect or than is necessary for immediate hub functionality, creating a risk of data minimization and purpose-limitation violations.
assumptions: Users may expect transient processing rather than long-term detailed retention of raw events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/non-compliance-related node for excessive collection/retention; numbering may be approximate.

title: Residents may be unaware that detailed sensor events are persistently logged
description: If the hub silently writes sensor events to a local datastore, occupants and visitors may not understand that their movements and entries/exits are being recorded and retained, undermining transparency and informed awareness.
assumptions: The system does not clearly notify users or visitors about local logging behavior and retention.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node id; exact numbering may vary.

title: Retention of raw home-event logs may violate privacy obligations
description: Persistently storing detailed home sensor events without clear retention limits, purpose specification, access controls, or user controls may conflict with applicable privacy requirements such as data minimization, storage limitation, and transparency obligations.
assumptions: Relevant legal, contractual, or policy obligations apply to the household system or service provider managing the hub.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Sensitive video clips disclosed in transit to cloud storage
description: Recorded camera clips may be intercepted or exposed while being uploaded from the Home Hub to Cloud Video Storage, revealing occupants, visitors, routines, and activities.
assumptions: The upload traverses a network where transport protection could be absent, weak, or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for disclosure on a data flow may differ.

title: Stored cloud video clips exposed to unauthorized parties
description: Once uploaded, cloud-stored camera clips may be accessible to unauthorized internal staff, attackers, or other tenants if access control, segregation, or encryption at rest are insufficient.
assumptions: Cloud Video Storage retains uploaded clips and may be reachable by multiple administrative or service components.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for disclosure from a datastore may differ.

title: Cloud-stored clips enable linkage of events and household behavior over time
description: Accumulated uploaded clips can be linked across timestamps, cameras, accounts, or devices to build a detailed picture of household routines, presence patterns, and relationships.
assumptions: The cloud service stores metadata such as account identifiers, timestamps, device identifiers, or camera identifiers alongside clips.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort estimate for linkability due to persistent identifiers and correlated records.

title: Uploaded clips and metadata identify residents or visitors
description: Video content and associated metadata can directly or indirectly identify household members, visitors, and the specific home, especially when faces, voices, interiors, timestamps, or location-linked account data are present.
assumptions: Clips contain recognizable people or contextual details and are associated with a customer account or device.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for identifiability from content and metadata.

title: Cloud retention of uploaded clips enables excessive profiling and detectability of home occupancy
description: Retained video clips and upload patterns can reveal whether occupants are home, asleep, away, receiving visitors, or following recurring routines, making private activities detectable beyond what is necessary for storage.
assumptions: The service retains clips and/or upload metadata over time and can observe timing and frequency of uploads.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; detectability and content-derived inference can overlap with disclosure/linkability.

title: Users may be unaware that clips are uploaded and retained in the cloud
description: Residents or visitors may not understand that locally recorded camera clips are automatically uploaded to cloud storage, how long they are retained, who can access them, or for what secondary purposes they may be used.
assumptions: Notice in setup, UI, or policy may be incomplete, unclear, or not visible to all affected individuals such as visitors.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for lack of awareness/transparency.

title: Cloud storage of home video may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: Uploading and retaining recorded clips in cloud storage may go beyond the consent given by residents or the expectations of visitors, especially if clips are reused for analytics, service improvement, law-enforcement response, or indefinite retention.
assumptions: Consent may be bundled, ambiguous, or absent for all data subjects appearing in clips; secondary use is possible.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for non-compliance/consent and purpose-limitation issues.

title: Insufficient upload logging undermines accountability for clip transfers
description: If the Home Hub does not reliably log what clips were uploaded, when, and under which account or policy, it may be difficult to demonstrate compliance, investigate disputes, or prove whether a particular clip transfer occurred.
assumptions: Audit trails may be incomplete, mutable, or not exposed to users/controllers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for non-repudiation/accountability-related privacy concerns.

title: Linkability of repeated motion alerts to the same household/device
description: Real-time motion alerts sent from the Home Hub to the backend may carry stable device, household, account, or network identifiers that allow the backend or anyone with access to backend-side telemetry to link multiple alerts over time to the same home and build a longitudinal activity profile.
assumptions: The alert contains or is accompanied by persistent identifiers, metadata, or routing information that remain stable across events.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability of messages/events may vary.

title: Identifiability of residents from motion-alert content and metadata
description: Even if the alert is only a motion event, timestamps, device identifiers, household identifiers, IP addresses, and location/account context at the backend can make the household or specific residents identifiable, especially when combined with subscriber records.
assumptions: The backend can associate incoming alerts with customer accounts, addresses, or other identifying records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact identifiability subtree may differ depending on whether identifiers are explicit or inferred via metadata.

title: Disclosure of occupancy patterns through stored or observable motion alerts
description: Motion alerts reveal when movement occurs in the home. If the backend stores, logs, monitors, or exposes these alerts, it can disclose sensitive occupancy and behavior patterns such as presence at home, sleep/wake routines, or absences.
assumptions: Alerts are retained, logged, accessible to operators, or otherwise observable beyond the minimum necessary processing path.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact disclosure subtree may depend on whether disclosure is in transit, at rest, or via logging/monitoring.

title: Detectability of in-home activity from the existence and timing of alerts
description: The mere presence, frequency, and timing of messages from the Home Hub to the backend can allow an observer with access to traffic metadata or backend event streams to detect that motion occurred, even without reading full payload contents.
assumptions: An observer can access traffic metadata, message timing, sizes, or backend event notifications.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact detectability subtree may distinguish content-independent traffic analysis from explicit event signaling.

title: Unawareness of backend processing of real-time motion events
description: Residents may be unaware that each motion event is forwarded to the mobile app backend, potentially logged, analyzed, retained, or used for secondary purposes such as analytics, service improvement, or incident investigation.
assumptions: User notices and controls do not fully explain the transmission, retention, and downstream uses of motion alerts.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact unawareness subtree may depend on whether the issue is lack of notice, opacity of purpose, or hidden recipients.

title: Non-compliance risk from excessive collection or retention of motion-alert data
description: Forwarding real-time motion alerts to the backend may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, retention limitation, or transparency obligations if more event detail than necessary is transmitted, retained too long, or reused beyond delivering the alerting service.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements constrain collection, retention, and secondary use of occupancy-related event data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact non-compliance subtree depends on the governing legal/control framework.

title: Repudiation gaps around who triggered or received a motion alert
description: If the system lacks trustworthy records and clear attribution, parties may later dispute whether a motion alert was generated, forwarded, received, or acted upon. In privacy terms, weak accountability can hinder data-subject rights handling, incident investigation, and proving appropriate processing.
assumptions: Audit trails, timestamps, integrity protection, or attribution mechanisms are incomplete or not trustworthy.
uncertainty_note: Applicability of non-repudiation to this privacy flow is somewhat context-dependent; node id is best-effort.

title: Notification content may disclose occupancy or in-home activity to unintended viewers
description: A motion-detected push notification can reveal that movement occurred at the home, exposing sensitive information about presence, routines, or activity inside the residence if seen on a lock screen, shared device, or by someone with access to notification channels.
assumptions: The notification contains explicit text such as 'Motion detected' and may be displayed on the phone lock screen or wearable companion devices.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure via message contents, but exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Repeated motion notifications can enable linking of homeowner behavior patterns
description: A series of motion-detected notifications sent over time can be correlated to infer the homeowner's daily routines, occupancy patterns, sleep schedule, or travel periods. Even if each notification is individually innocuous, together they can link events into a behavioral profile.
assumptions: An observer, notification service, or compromised device can access multiple notifications over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability across multiple events; exact node id may differ in the official threat tree.

title: Push delivery metadata can identify the homeowner as occupant of a monitored property
description: Sending the notification to a specific mobile device or push token can identify the recipient as associated with a particular home, security system, or monitored event stream. This may reveal that the person owns, occupies, or is responsible for the property.
assumptions: Push tokens, account identifiers, or backend routing metadata are associated with a specific homeowner account.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed estimate for identifiability through identifiers/metadata.

title: Lack of evidence about notification delivery or viewing can create repudiation issues
description: If the system does not maintain trustworthy records of whether the motion notification was sent, delivered, or opened, parties may later dispute whether the homeowner was informed about the event. This can affect accountability for privacy-relevant actions triggered by the alert.
assumptions: The system relies on notification delivery as a meaningful privacy/security communication and lacks tamper-resistant audit logs.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow than disclosure; node id is approximate.

title: Homeowner may be unaware that notification previews expose sensitive home-event data
description: The homeowner may not understand that motion alerts can appear on lock screens, wearables, or mirrored devices, causing sensitive household activity information to be exposed beyond the intended recipient.
assumptions: Default device/app settings allow preview text or cross-device notification mirroring.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of user awareness about privacy-relevant data exposure; exact node id may vary.

title: Notification delivery may be incompatible with data minimization or confidentiality expectations
description: Including detailed motion-event information in push notifications may violate privacy requirements or user preferences if less revealing messaging would suffice, or if notifications are sent through third-party push providers without adequate safeguards.
assumptions: Applicable policy, consent choice, or regulatory requirement limits disclosure of in-home activity data in transient notifications or via third-party processors.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends heavily on jurisdiction, policy, and implementation details; node id is approximate.

title: Analytics payload may enable linkage of user sessions or cohorts across contexts
description: Even if described as aggregated device-usage analytics, the backend may share stable cohort keys, device characteristics, timestamps, campaign identifiers, or other quasi-identifiers that allow the cloud analytics vendor to link records belonging to the same user, device, household, or app account over time or across datasets.
assumptions: The shared analytics include repeated observations, metadata, or segmentation fields beyond strictly anonymous one-off counts.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability from a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree labeling may vary.

title: Vendor may infer behavior patterns or sensitive traits from aggregated analytics
description: The cloud analytics vendor may use the received usage aggregates to infer user interests, routines, location patterns, health-related behavior, or other sensitive attributes, especially when combined with its own telemetry or third-party datasets.
assumptions: The vendor has additional datasets or sufficient granularity in the aggregates to support inference.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability/inference risk; exact subtree may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Analytics sharing may disclose information to an external party beyond user expectations
description: Sending device-usage analytics to an external analytics vendor discloses personal or group-level behavioral information to a third party. Even if aggregated, the disclosure may exceed what users reasonably expect or what is necessary for the stated service purpose.
assumptions: The analytics are derived from user/device activity and the vendor is a separate controller or processor with access to the data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node chosen generically for third-party data sharing.

title: Users may be unaware that backend analytics are shared with a cloud vendor
description: The transfer may lack sufficient transparency, making users unaware of what analytics are sent, at what granularity, for which purposes, and with which downstream recipients or retention periods.
assumptions: Privacy notices, in-app disclosures, or just-in-time notices are incomplete, unclear, or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact numbering may vary.

title: Sharing aggregated analytics with vendor may be incompatible with consent, purpose limitation, or minimization
description: The backend may transmit analytics to the vendor without a valid legal basis, outside the original purpose communicated to users, or with more detail than necessary. Aggregation alone does not guarantee compliance if the data remain personal or can be combined for profiling.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements impose constraints on consent, transparency, purpose limitation, minimization, retention, or cross-border transfers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node selected at a generic level; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Vendor may retain or repurpose analytics beyond the intended duration or purpose
description: Once received, the cloud analytics vendor may store the analytics longer than necessary, combine them with other customer data, or reuse them for product improvement, benchmarking, or model training, reducing the data subject's ability to control dissemination.
assumptions: Contractual and technical controls on retention, onward sharing, and secondary use are weak or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/dissemination-control-related node; exact node id may vary.

title: Stored video clip may be disclosed to an unauthorized backend context or requester
description: When the backend retrieves a stored video clip from cloud storage, insufficient authorization checks, overly broad service permissions, or weak binding between the clip and the authenticated homeowner request could cause the clip to be exposed beyond the intended recipient. Video footage from a home environment is highly privacy-sensitive and may reveal occupants, visitors, routines, and interior details.
assumptions: Cloud storage contains identifiable household video clips and the backend acts on behalf of a homeowner session or account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro disclosure subtree label may differ.

title: Backend retrieval of specific clips can reveal homeowner behavior and viewing interests
description: The act of requesting particular stored clips for playback can reveal which times, cameras, or events a homeowner is interested in. Observers of backend access patterns, logs, or internal analytics could infer occupancy patterns, incidents, or personal concerns from which videos are retrieved and when.
assumptions: Access metadata such as clip identifiers, timestamps, camera identifiers, or request timing is observable internally or by supporting services.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed estimate; exact LINDDUN Pro inference subtree mapping may vary.

title: Video retrieval events may be linkable across sessions or devices
description: If the backend uses stable account identifiers, device identifiers, or persistent request metadata when retrieving clips, multiple playback requests can be linked together. This can enable building a profile of a homeowner's habits, camera usage, and monitoring behavior over time.
assumptions: Retrieval requests carry persistent identifiers or are logged in a way that supports correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id from memory; exact linkability subtree node may differ.

title: Retrieval metadata may enable detection of homeowner presence, routines, or incidents
description: Even without viewing the clip contents, the timing and frequency of backend retrievals can allow an observer to detect sensitive facts, such as when the homeowner is away, when motion events occurred, or when unusual incidents prompted playback. This detection can arise from traffic analysis, logs, or monitoring of backend-storage interactions.
assumptions: An attacker or internal observer can access or infer retrieval timing, frequency, or clip-selection metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact detectability node id may differ; chosen as a best-fit estimate.

title: Stored video may be processed for playback without adequate consent, purpose limitation, or retention controls
description: Using stored home video for playback is expected by the homeowner, but the same retrieval path could also support secondary processing, broader internal access, or retention beyond what data subjects reasonably expect. If consent, transparency, or purpose limitation are not properly enforced, the flow may violate privacy obligations for residents, visitors, or bystanders captured in the clip.
assumptions: Video clips may contain personal data of multiple data subjects, not only the homeowner, and governance controls may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; non-compliance trees vary by obligation and exact legal/control context.
